objectives.wording: Define public health and use a community example to distinguish population prevention and service delivery.
Build a dated five-year timeline of major public health events using authoritative reports.
Analyze a documented local event by population affected, response and lessons for prevention.
Explain physical, mental, social and spiritual dimensions and compare determinants across settings.
Use an agent–host–environment model and a causal web to explain a multifactorial disease.
Map susceptibility, subclinical disease, clinical onset and outcomes for a representative condition.
Assign interventions to prevention levels and justify their timing.
Compare health promotion, education, IEC and behaviour change communication in a community scenario.
Plan education or counselling at individual, family and community levels using suitable objectives and delivery methods.
Choose and interpret representative mortality, morbidity, service and wellbeing indicators.
Interpret a dated Indian demographic profile and explain implications for service needs.
Explain the demographic cycle and distinguish demographic measures from vital statistics.
Use Indian data to explain population growth, age structure and consequences for services.
Demonstrate clear messaging, active listening and teach-back in simulation.
Demonstrate rapport, respect and shared decisions in a simulated encounter.
Perform a structured clinical, sociocultural and demographic assessment at individual, family and community levels.
Compare family structures and sociocultural influences and demonstrate use of a context-appropriate socioeconomic tool.
Use a simulated interview to identify barriers and map their effects on health-seeking decisions.
Explain how norms, group behaviour and relationships influence health behaviours and outcomes.
Connect poverty to health and explain how representative social security measures can reduce barriers.
Compare sources and health effects of air, water, noise and radiation hazards and identify preventive measures.
Compare sources, purification steps and quality checks and explain conservation and rainwater harvesting.
Trace transmission of representative diarrhoeal and hepatitis infections and identify points for prevention.
Compare safe handling and disposal approaches for solid waste, excreta and sewage.
Assess a representative dwelling against applicable standards and link ventilation, crowding and sanitation to health.
Connect vectors to transmission and explain surveillance and control using current Indian programme documents.
Identify representative public health vectors from specimens or images and match life stages to control measures.
Compare modes of action, application cycles and safe selection for representative settings.
Compare individual, group and mass methods by reach, participation and limitations.
Conduct a brief audience-appropriate health education session during simulation or a supervised posting and check understanding.
Demonstrate how to select indicators, collect data and interpret results for a simulated programme.
Match local food sources to nutrients and compare requirements by age, sex, activity and physiological state.
Demonstrate suitable dietary, anthropometric or other assessment methods for individuals, families and communities.
Complete a nutritional assessment and use the findings to propose a health-promoting diet.
Compare the epidemiology, assessment and prevention of protein-energy malnutrition in the community.
Compare the epidemiology and prevention of iron, zinc, iodine and vitamin deficiencies in the community.
Build a simulated family diet around locally available foods, affordability and individual needs.
Develop an individualized simulated diet plan for diabetes, hypertension or obesity using realistic substitutions.
Build vegetarian, ovo-vegetarian and non-vegetarian menus and check protein against the applicable ICMR–NIN reference.
Review a personal or simulated dietary record and identify realistic improvements and a follow-up measure.
Explain how a representative dietary change can support health promotion and disease prevention.
Role-play setting achievable dietary goals for diabetes, hypertension or obesity and check understanding.
Plan and deliver a short nutrition session for a community or NCD clinic and assess understanding.
Choose surveillance indicators and design culturally appropriate education and rehabilitation measures.
Use dated official documents to compare the national policy and programme objectives, beneficiaries and service delivery, including ICDS.
Identify contamination risks from preparation to storage and propose controls for a sample kitchen.
Compare food fortification methods and their public health uses.
Explain the functions and risks of food additives and the public health consequences of adulteration.
Demonstrate holds, attachment and manual milk expression using models.
Use case prompts to explain breastfeeding and complementary feeding across infancy.
Use a simulated encounter to assess attachment and position and demonstrate corrections with teach-back.
Counsel a simulated caregiver on breastfeeding and agree a feasible plan.
Use an age-specific scenario to discuss the eight food groups, meal frequency, quantities and texture.
Use national guidance to counsel a simulated caregiver and adapt food choices to culture and budget.
Counsel a simulated caregiver on complementary feeding and agree a feasible plan.
Compare sample products using serving size, ingredients and nutrient declarations and explain the comparison to a simulated patient.
Turn a community health problem into a focused, answerable research question.
Prepare a brief protocol specifying design, sampling, measures, analysis and ethics.
Collect or review sample data, classify variables, analyse and interpret findings and present them in an appropriate format.
Import a sample dataset, check variable types and demonstrate a basic analysis.
Summarize a dataset using suitable numerical and graphical measures and interpret the distribution.
Use software to clean a sample line list and display time, place and person patterns.
Choose a basic test for representative study designs, check its assumptions and interpret the result.
Demonstrate common sampling methods and summarize a dataset using frequency, central tendency and dispersion.
Define epidemiology and apply its principles to describing and investigating a community health problem.
Map communicable transmission and noncommunicable risk pathways to appropriate prevention and control measures.
Compare surveillance, surveys, registries and routine records by coverage, timeliness and limitations.
Calculate and interpret incidence, prevalence and selected mortality measures from supplied data.
Compare descriptive, observational analytic and experimental designs and match each to a research question.
Assess whether screening is justified and interpret test performance and likely consequences in a sample population.
Work through a simulated outbreak from case definition and line listing to hypothesis, control and communication.
Choose immediate and longer-term control measures for a simulated epidemic and explain their rationale.
Compare operational and communication problems in outbreaks and propose preventive measures.
Interpret an observed association and assess bias, confounding and evidence for causation.
Appraise a supplied study for design, bias, results and applicability.
Use representative primary care cases to connect epidemiology, essential tests, prevention and control.
Compare risk patterns, essential primary care tests and control strategies for diabetes, hypertension, stroke, obesity and cancer.
Use dated official documents to compare case prevention, detection, treatment and referral across representative programmes.
Deliver a simulated training session on surveillance, control, treatment or referral and health education.
Map collection, validation, reporting and feedback and explain how managers use the information.
Calculate and interpret birth, death and fertility rates from supplied data.
Compare census, SRS, NFHS and national sample surveys by purpose, coverage and limitations.
Compare plausible drivers of declining sex ratios and explain social and health implications using dated data.
Compare voluntary, rights-based approaches to reducing unmet need and supporting population stabilization.
Use the official policy to summarize its objectives and relate them to representative indicators.
Interpret dated reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health indicators and identify service gaps.
Elicit local customs concerning pregnancy, delivery, lactation and feeding and distinguish supportive from potentially harmful practices.
Choose screening approaches for representative high-risk groups and common problems and explain follow-up.
Map safe-motherhood interventions across pregnancy and childbirth.
Map child-survival interventions across the newborn period and childhood.
Use current official documents to explain the Universal Immunization Programme.
Use current official documents to explain integrated management of neonatal and childhood illness.
Compare methods by effectiveness, suitability, advantages and limitations in representative cases.
Map programme organization, delivery and follow-up and explain operational responsibilities.
Relate adolescent development to clinical and counselling needs and use applicable reproductive and sexual health pathways.
Analyze how gender barriers affect health access and propose measures that support agency and equity.
Coordinate a supervised or simulated clinic session covering service allocation, referrals and follow-up.
Use exposure history and presenting findings to recognize representative occupational illnesses, including agricultural exposures.
Use current official scheme documents to explain coverage, benefits and service access in a simulated case.
Match representative hazards and risk factors to controls using the hierarchy of controls.
Assess a sample workstation and recommend changes to fit the worker and reduce strain.
Compare common occupational disorders in health professionals and explain prevention and management pathways.
Design and run a simulated workplace response covering surveillance, incident management and referral.
Describe components of geriatric services and map care from community support to referral.
Compare representative chronic, functional, sensory, cognitive and psychosocial needs.
Select representative preventive measures based on function, risks and preferences.
Use dated official guidance to map programme services across levels of care.
Perform a simulated assessment of function, falls, cognition, nutrition and support and prioritize follow-up.
Define disaster management and explain how hazard, exposure, vulnerability and capacity shape impact.
Map mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery to a representative disaster.
Compare Indian and international examples by causes, impacts and prevention opportunities.
Use official material to explain NDMA responsibilities and coordination with state and local authorities.
Participate in a tabletop exercise covering triage, communication, resource allocation and referral.
Classify representative hospital waste streams by source and hazard.
Match waste categories to treatment options and explain their limitations.
Use official Indian biomedical waste rules to map institutional duties.
Sort simulated waste at the point of generation using the applicable colour coding and sharps precautions.
Explain mental health, wellbeing and the influence of social and environmental factors.
Recognize early warning signs and identify presentations that require urgent assessment in simulated cases.
Assess simulated individual, family and community situations and identify initial support and referral needs.
Use official programme documents to map community, district and referral services.
Define health planning and distinguish needs, priorities, objectives and resources.
Apply the planning cycle to a sample community health problem.
Use official policy documents to compare national priorities and how they translate into planning.
Develop an implementation and evaluation plan based on disease burden, resources and measurable outcomes.
Compare representative scheduling, resource allocation and monitoring techniques and select one for a service problem.
Compare cost-effectiveness, cost-utility and cost–benefit approaches and interpret a simplified planning decision.
Describe how population needs shape preventive, promotive, curative and rehabilitative care.
Explain core principles and components and apply them to a local service scenario.
Combine sample demographic, health and service data to identify and rank community problems.
Relate Indian health policy to historical Millennium Development Goals and corresponding health indicators.
Map public and private delivery across community, primary, secondary and tertiary levels.
Trace a simulated patient pathway and identify referral, follow-up and coordination responsibilities.
Explain how cross-border health risks and shared resources create a role for international cooperation.
Use a tabletop scenario to allocate national and international roles for surveillance, prevention and response.
Compare representative agencies by mandate, functions and modes of support.
Explain the purpose and selection criteria of an essential medicines list.
Relate an essential medicines list to availability, rational prescribing and service delivery.
Estimate essential medicine requirements from consumption or morbidity data, allowing for stock and lead time.
Recognize warning signs of suspect products and explain prevention and reporting pathways.
Identify applicable official legal sources and explain their relevance to a simulated public health decision.
